question.text: Mr. Sharma, a retired professional, sold his equity mutual fund units (STT paid) after 15 months and made a total Long-Term Capital Gain of Rs. 2,25,000 in the financial year. Under the equity-oriented LTCG rules in the NISM Series V-B workbook (12-month holding qualifies as long-term; the first Rs. 1.25 lakh of equity LTCG in a financial year is exempt), what is the taxable amount of LTCG on which tax has to be computed?

explanation.text: The Logic: The NISM Series V-B workbook (pp.120-121) states that equity-oriented mutual fund units held for more than 12 months qualify as long-term, and that the first Rs. 1.25 lakh of long-term capital gain on equity-oriented funds in a financial year is exempt. Mr. Sharma held for 15 months (>12 months) and his total LTCG is Rs. 2,25,000. Taxable LTCG = Rs. 2,25,000 - Rs. 1,25,000 (exemption) = Rs. 1,00,000. The question now asks only for the taxable amount, which is sourced directly to p121. The Trap: Option B forgets to deduct the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption. Option C confuses the exempt threshold (Rs. 1.25 lakh) with the taxable amount. Option D wrongly treats the whole gain as exempt. The audit flagged the original item because it asked for the rupee LTCG tax (Rs. 12,500), which requires the 12.5% rate that the cached workbook pages 120-121 do not explicitly show. Note: The original stem asked for the rupee tax amount, which depended on a 12.5% LTCG rate that could not be verified from the cached NISM Series V-B pp.120-121 text. The item has been narrowed to test only the workbook-supported Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption (the rule expressly on p.121), making the Rs. 1,00,000 taxable LTCG uniquely correct.
